# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-8 (Extended v89)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 2, following day after funeral)**: Valjean and Cosette established in convent garden; Valjean working as assistant gardener alongside Fauchelevent; Cosette attending as convent scholar. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak; body placed in vault beneath grand altar during 11 p.m.–midnight procedures; **Following day (sun declining, afternoon/evening)**: Funeral procession departing toward Vaugirard cemetery; **procession reached cemetery at dusk**; sun touching dome, cemetery closing in five minutes. **CURRENT (day after funeral)**: Valjean and Cosette integrated into convent life; nuns observe "two men digging side by side" under trees; children play in garden; carts pass well; normal rhythms resumed.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil; **English harbor towns**: Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven, and named individuals (Luvie, Wilwick, Gadrek Prydenridge, Isric, Jotho, Tatho Brackick, Harine Lindmere, Pelde Stenson, Pelde Stenworth, Yera Stenworth, Yewyn Haskick, Orrald the Younger, Davus Stenworth, Ismira Stenson, etc.). Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars (squares less than 1.5 inches diagonal) riveted by clenched-fist fastenings; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters reinforced with gingerbread-yellow wooden beams, always closed; behind shutters: nun's voice screened by iron grating and plate with thousand holes; slat opens revealing nun's mouth and chin only, covered with black veil, guimpe, shroud. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Lower hall of church communicates with street, no men enter except doctor of dead; **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient cemetery outside regulations, has special Permission from Prefecture for nuns to be taken there at nightfall; venerable enclosure planted like old-fashioned French garden with straight alleys, box, thuya-trees, holly, ancient tombs beneath aged cypress-trees, very tall grass; tragic and lugubrious in evening; cemetery closed at dusk; accessed via grand alley through cypress-trees, narrows to waste land and thicket. **Boulevard du Maine**: Route of funeral procession. **Rue Chemin-Vert**: Location of deaf fruit-seller (good old friend of Fauchelevent), who provided bed for Cosette overnight. **Grave-digger's dwelling (Vaugirard cemetery)**: Unfurnished garret; packing-case as commode; butter-pot as drinking-fountain; straw mattress as bed; thin woman and children piled on tattered carpet fragment; shows signs of desperate search. **Garden hut (convent end)**: Built of old rubbish, existed 1845; three utterly bare chambers; principal chamber given to Valjean (opposed in vain); walls ornamented with two nails for knee-cap and basket, and Royalist bank-note of '93 above chimney-piece.

## Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration
[Same as before—order lineage, dress, austerity, vows, operational rules, reparation practice, possessions rule, hourly bells, chanting, men allowed; no mirrors; girls conscious of beauty do not become nuns; vocation voluntary in inverse proportion to good looks; convent has preference for plain girls]

**MOTHER CRUCIFIXION'S DEATH AND FUNERAL COMPLETION**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak (Winter Year 2). Retained consciousness to last moment, spoke to community then to angels, gave final commands. Prioress described her death as "precious"—smiled, community felt she was regaining life in God. Sisters laid out body. **VAULT BURIAL EXECUTED** (11 p.m.–midnight, same night): Fauchelevent closed coffin; sisters carried coffin to chapel; office for dead said; community returned to cloister. Fauchelevent came with iron bar; Mother Precentors and Mother Ascension present; vault opened beneath grand altar, coffin lowered, vault closed again—no trace, government has no suspicion. Doctor signed death passport. **FUNERAL PROCESSION** (following day, afternoon/evening): Undertaker company brought empty coffin for appearance; hearse ornamented with skulls, cross-bones, tears; coffin covered with white cloth, large black cross; mourning-coach with priest in surplice and choir boy in red cap; two undertaker's men in gray uniforms trimmed with black walked beside hearse; Fauchelevent limped behind in laborer's garments; procession heading toward Vaugirard cemetery; soil light and wet with winter rains, clogged hearse wheels, retarded speed. **ARRIVAL AT CEMETERY**: Hearse skirted cypress-trees, quitted grand alley, turned into narrow alley, entered waste land, plunged into thicket, indicating proximity of burial place. Sun touching dome at arrival; cemetery closed in five minutes.

## Jean Valjean's Escape, Integration, and Psychological State
**ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Valjean hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank. Felt carried out and driven off. Divined progression from diminution in jolting when leaving pavements for earth road; dull noise crossing Bridge of Austerlitz; at first halt entering cemetery; at second halt recognizing burial imminent. Possessed gloomy talent—understood contracting to fit diameter of escape; could live long time in box, find air where none exists, economize breath for hours, stifle without dying. Demonstrated composure and coolness in crisis—powerful tranquility contagious to others. **COSETTE'S RETRIEVAL**: After cemetery procedures, Fauchelevent and Valjean (emerged from grave after burial) went to fetch Cosette from fruit-seller in Rue du Chemin-Vert, where she had been deposited previous day. Cosette passed twenty-four hours trembling silently, understanding nothing; trembled so she wept; neither eaten nor slept; fruit-seller plied hundred questions without obtaining reply except melancholy, unvarying gaze; Cosette betrayed nothing of what seen/heard in last two days; divined passing through crisis; deeply conscious need to "be good"; fear is mute; no one guards secret like child. **CURRENT STATUS (Day After Funeral)**: Integrated into convent life as assistant gardener; inhabits old hut at garden end in company with Fauchelevent; shares principal chamber with Fauchelevent (Fauchelevent received it by force; Valjean opposed in vain). Works in garden every day, made himself very useful; formerly pruner of trees; gladly found himself gardener once more; knows all sorts of secrets and receipts for agriculture; turned to advantage—almost all orchard trees ungrafted and wild; he budded them and made them produce excellent fruit. Receives visits from Cosette daily (permitted one hour); at appointed hour she flies to hut; when she enters lowly cabin, fills it with paradise; Valjean blossoms out and feels happiness increase with happiness afforded Cosette; joy which we inspire returns to us more radiant than ever. At recreation hours watches her running and playing in distance, distinguishes her laugh from rest.

**PSYCHOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT**: Convent contributed like Cosette to uphold and complete Bishop's work in Valjean. Virtue adjoins pride; bridge built by devil exists there. Had been unconsciously perhaps tolerably near that side and bridge when Providence cast his lot in convent; so long as compared himself only to Bishop, regarded himself unworthy and remained humble; but for some time past comparing himself to men in general, and pride beginning to spring up. Meditation on two places of captivity: in youth, beginning of life, beheld galleys—frightful place, terrible place, whose severities appeared iniquity of justice, crime of law; now after galleys, sees cloister; when meditated how formed part of galleys and now so to speak spectator of cloister, confronted two in own mind with anxiety. Recalled former companions: wretched, rose at dawn, toiled until night, hardly permitted sleep, lay on camp beds with mattresses two inches thick, rooms heated only harshest months, clothed in frightful red blouses, allowed linen trousers in hottest weather or woollen carter's blouse when very cold, drank no wine, ate no meat except on fatigue duty, lived nameless, designated only by numbers, converted into ciphers, downcast eyes, lowered voices, shorn heads, beneath cudgel and in disgrace. Contrasts: on one hand miasms; on other, ineffable perfume; on one hand moral pest guarded from sight, penned up under cannon, literally devouring plague-stricken victims; on other, chaste flame of all souls on same hearth; there darkness; here shadow filled with gleams of light and gleams full of radiance.

## Cosette's Integration and Emotional State
**INITIAL STATE**: Cosette knew nothing; could say nothing; would not have said anything in any case. Nothing trains children to silence like unhappiness. Had suffered so much, feared everything, even to speak or breathe. Single word had so often brought down avalanche upon her. Hardly begun to regain confidence since with Jean Valjean. **CONVENT INTEGRATION**: Speedily became accustomed to convent. Only regretted Catherine, but dared not say so. Once said to Jean Valjean: "Father, if I had known, I would have brought her away with me." Thinks herself Jean Valjean's daughter (natural assumption; author notes she knew nothing so could say nothing; would not have said anything anyway). Became convent scholar; received new garments (garb of pupils of house). **VALJEAN'S PRESERVATION**: Valjean succeeded in getting them to restore garments she laid aside—same mourning suit made her put on when quitted Thénardiers' inn; not very threadbare even now. Valjean locked up these garments plus stockings and shoes with quantity of camphor and all aromatics convents abound in, in little valise he procured. Set valise on chair near his bed; always carried key about his person. Cosette asked him: "Father, what is there in that box which smells so good?" **DAILY INTERACTION**: At appointed hour flies to hut; fills it with paradise; adored him because sisters melancholy and he kind; makes comparisons; watches her running and playing in distance at recreation hours; distinguishes her laugh from rest.

## Fauchelevent's Crucial Role and Expanded Status
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821 or earlier) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour to traverse short distances; complains of aching back as usual. **COSETTE PLAN EXECUTED**: Used service door opening on courtyard; knocked, porter opened; placed Cosette in vintage basket on back, covered—"Father Fauchelevent goes out with his basket—perfectly natural"; left her with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert (good old friend) who provided little bed; told fruit-seller in shout that child was his niece, to keep her until following day. **VALJEAN PLAN EXECUTED**: Placed Valjean in coffin; transported coffin in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery with Valjean inside. **CEMETERY OPERATIONS**: At cemetery, Father Mestienne (grave-digger) dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug of red wine, Surêne Paris wine). Fauchelevent offered drink to new grave-digger "conscript" but avoided explaining payment. New grave-digger claimed accepted Mestienne's reversion; works scrivener's stall in market Rue de Sèvres (Umbrella Market), writes love letters to raw soldiers mornings, digs graves evenings. **CRITICAL COMPLICATION RESOLVED**: Grave-digger lost card (cemetery entry authorization). Without card, could not return. Fauchelevent revealed he found card on ground after grave-digger left, buried corpse, filled grave, did work himself; porter would return card; conscript wouldn't pay fifteen francs. **FAUCHELEVENT'S COMPOSURE AND PEACE OF MIND**: Though souls troubled even when recovered, something uncanny about him—sinister bewilderment inspired by place, perfectly composed; knew grave-digger Gribier wouldn't arrive (conscript at home searching lodgings for card, which Fauchelevent carried); cemetery closed; no apprehension of interference. **CHARACTER AND RECOMPENSE**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; speaks freely; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass of good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude toward end of days. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; rendered good action absolutely necessary; enlisted self-devotion, good will, old rustic cunning. **TRIPLE SUCCESS**: Won triple success—in eyes of Jean Valjean (saved and sheltered); in those of grave-digger Gribier (who said to himself: "He spared me that fine"); with convent (enabled to retain coffin of Mother Crucifixion under altar, eluded Cæsar and satisfied God). **RECOMPENSE**: Father Fauchelevent received other recompense in addition to glory (of which knew nothing); made him happy; had much less work since shared; very fond of snuff, found presence of M. Madeleine advantage—used three times as much as previously, in infinitely more luxurious manner, since M. Madeleine paid for it. **CURRENT STATUS**: Lives in garden hut with Valjean; continues gardening work; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's full presence; only known ally and protector; nuns do not suspect him leaves garden regularly (elders always sent for outside errands, never younger man); eyes fixed on God do not spy; nuns occupied in keeping watch on each other, paid no heed.

## Javert's Pursuit and Ongoing Investigation
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS** (January 1823): When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail, Javert attached to Paris police force. **NEWSPAPER REPORT** (December 1823): Newspaper announced Valjean's death; Javert remarked "That's a good entry." **REACTIVATION**: Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived Javert's memory; suspected Valjean sought daughter. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead was magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern, led astray. **STRATEGIC PURSUIT**: Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily (considered it risky, preferred gloating anticipation). **CURRENT STATUS** (Winter Year 2): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. Free press embarrasses police; arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers; police agents afraid of mistakes.

## Narrative Commentary and Moral Themes
Author remarks burial of Mother Crucifixion under altar of convent is perfectly venial offence—one of faults which resemble duty. Nuns committed it without difficulty, even with applause of own consciences. In cloister, "government" is only intermeddling with authority, always questionable. Rule takes precedence over code. Tribute to Cæsar never anything but remnants of tribute to God. Prince is nothing in presence of principle. Public order had no doubt been deeply disturbed by coffin containing body in Petit-Picpus and coffin without body in Vaugirard cemetery, but no one aware of it. Notes souls troubled; convent contributed to complete Bishop's work in Valjean; danger of pride in comparative virtue; contrast between galley-life and cloister-life illuminates nature of captivity itself.
